name: Speak 714
label: Revelation
lede: A late-'90s Orange County band built from Ignite, Pennywise, Slapshot and No For An Answer parts, fronted by a singer who recorded it after having his jaw wired shut and still refuses to say the area code.

eras.title: Thirst, then Speak, then a phone code
eras.text: Joe Foster of Ignite and Unity came to Dan O'Mahony, ex-No For An Answer and 411, with music already recorded. Players from Pennywise, Straight Faced and Slapshot filled out the record, and the band spent one furious year on the road.

years.h: Joe Foster brings Dan O'Mahony a finished set of songs
years.p: Guitarist Joe Foster approaches Dan O'Mahony with music already tracked by Pennywise's Randy Bradbury, Straight Faced's Sam Marrs and drummer Doug McKinnon of Slapshot and [[The Vandals|f54fc7c3-3a40-4f26-83cf-328d9b097e93]].

q: to this day you will never hear me include the '714'
years.h: Why Dan O'Mahony won't say Speak 714
years.p: The band starts as Thirst, then becomes Speak after Dan O'Mahony's forearm tattoo. Both names are taken by other bands, so the Orange County area code 714 gets bolted on.
years.xp: O'Mahony told No Echo in 2025 that the name change was a real pain, and that he still never includes the 714 when he talks about the band.

q: a Las Vegas brawl that didn't exactly go my way
years.h: Dan O'Mahony's jaw is broken in a Las Vegas brawl
years.p: Before Knee Deep in Guilt is finished, Dan O'Mahony has his jaw broken in a Las Vegas fight he says didn't go his way. It's wired shut, and the album waits six weeks.

years.src: Visions · Revelation Records pressing history · No Echo
years.p: Ten songs in about 21 minutes, co-produced by Dan O'Mahony and Joe Foster. Germany's Visions called it a really great record and hoped the band would last.
years.xp: Revelation's first vinyl run was 110 copies on tan. In Europe it came out through SPV.

years.h: Speak 714 tour the US twice and Europe once in a year
years.p: Speak 714 fit two US tours and a European tour into the same year. Dan O'Mahony calls the headlining runs in the States and Europe a privilege.

years.h: Live at the Princeton Arts Council, May 16, 1998
yt: Live at the Princeton Arts Council, May 16, 1998

eras.title: New players, same singer
eras.text: The friction between Dan O'Mahony and Joe Foster broke the original band apart. O'Mahony made one more Speak 714 record with a new line-up, and then it faded out.

years.src: No Echo: Speak 714 · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: The Scum Also Rises, after O'Mahony and Foster split · REV 72
years.p: Conflict between Dan O'Mahony and Joe Foster reshapes Speak 714. Chris Lisk, Kevin Panter, Eryc Simmerer and Jeff Baker play on the EP; Simmerer wrote the music for Amsterdam.
years.xp: Revelation pressed the first run on yellow vinyl, 180 copies. After about a year of intense activity, the band came apart gradually rather than with a last show.

eras.title: No demand, no reunion
eras.text: Speak 714 never came back. Dan O'Mahony and Doug McKinnon did keep playing together, in Done Dying and later Shiners Club.

years.h: Dan O'Mahony and Doug McKinnon regroup in [[Done Dying|f17a4ac7-c333-4c13-8a23-886bc984a81e]]
years.p: The Speak 714 singer and drummer start Done Dying, which Dan O'Mahony calls a band of reunion-age players refusing to be a reunion band.

years.h: Dan O'Mahony looks back on Speak 714 for No Echo
years.p: Asked in 2025 whether Speak 714 would play again, Dan O'Mahony can't imagine there ever being much demand.
